content: For one-way server-to-client progress on long-running jobs, SSE is the simplest transport: it rides plain HTTP, needs no protocol upgrade, and the browser EventSource handles reconnection automatically, which WebSockets and long polling both require you to hand-roll. WebSockets only pay for themselves when the client also pushes continuously. Guidance is explicit: if only the server pushes use SSE; if both push use WebSockets; do not start with long polling. For a local single-user app the operative constraint is implementation overhead, not scale - and simple interval polling of a status endpoint remains defensible when updates are coarse-grained (a handful of state transitions), since it needs no streaming infrastructure at all and degrades trivially.
